Subject: Elevated 5xx/timeouts on rw15b — interim mitigation and recovery update

Hi team (Acme),

We’re reaching out to let you know we detected an uptick in 5xx and timeout responses for the rw15b model starting ~14:30 PDT today. Impact has been intermittent — elevated tail latency and some requests returning 5xx errors for longer sequences and bursty traffic patterns.

What we know so far:
- Start window: ~14:25–14:40 PDT (we've attached a timeline).
- Error class: 5xx timeouts originating from the rw15b serving fleet (model-level).
- Customer-visible impact: increased latency and a small fraction (~0.7%) of requests returning 5xx for affected prefixes.

Immediate actions we’ve taken:
- Rolled a short-term routing policy to prefer rw15b-v2 (compatible variant) for production traffic to reduce exposure.
- Scoped affected nodes out of the primary rw15b pool for deeper diagnostics.
- Collected and attached aggregated inference logs and a CSV timeline for your ops team.

Next steps and ask from Acme:
- Can you share any long-running prompt patterns or batched workflows from your side that map to 14:00–15:00 PDT? That will help correlation.

We know reliability is critical and we’ll send updates as we triage. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll prioritize minimizing further impact.

— Kimberly Park

Quick update from infra diagnostics (summary):
- Observed increased KV cache churn on rw15b nodes serving long-prefix requests; eviction rate spiked ~3.5x during the window.
- Scheduler logs show a regression in the continuous-batching path that can lead to head-of-line stalls when eviction <-> batch refill overlap occurs (rare race under bursty long-sequence workloads).
- Error traces correlate with a threadpool starvation window that causes amortized per-request latency to exceed the timeout threshold.

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Routing pref changed earlier to rw15b-v2 (less aggressive caching strategy) — error rate dropped to baseline within ~8 minutes after routing change.
- Throttled ETL-style clients that were identified via request fingerprinting (temporary).

Planned fix:
- Priyom has a patch that adds an eviction backoff and a small scheduler yield; we plan a canary deploy in the next 45–60 minutes (RW-9876).

I’ll post the canary results and the exact commit id once the deploy completes.

— Neha
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: RW15b incident — recovery confirmation and next steps

Hi Mark / Acme team,

Update and brief post-incident note:

What happened (short):
- A scheduler/regression + KV cache churn under bursty, long-sequence workloads caused transient threadpool starvation on a subset of rw15b nodes. That combination produced elevated tail latency and a small increase in 5xx/timeouts.

What we did:
- Immediate routing to rw15b-v2 to reduce exposure.
- Scoped affected nodes out of the rw15b pool and collected logs (attached).
- Throttled identified ETL-style clients for the short window.
- Deployed a targeted patch (canary -> progressive rollout) that introduces an eviction backoff and a scheduler yield to prevent the race.

Result:
- Error rate returned to baseline within ~10 minutes of the routing change; full rollout of the fix completed at 01:50 UTC.
- We validated production traffic across a representative ~2 hour window; no reoccurrence observed.

Impact:
- Customer-visible: short window of increased latency and ~0.7% request error rate for affected traffic. No data loss.

Next steps and follow-up:
- We’re preparing a short postmortem doc (internal + customer-facing) with timeline, root cause, and long-term mitigations (capacity-aware scheduler fixes and additional KV cache metrics).
- JIRA: RW-9876 will track the patch and follow-ups (link above).
- I’ve attached the aggregated logs and a timeline CSV for your ops team.

If you’d like a quick run-through of the postmortem once it’s ready, I can schedule a 30-min call with our SRE and product engineering leads.

Again — apologies for the disruption and thanks for your patience. We’ll share the customer-facing postmortem within 48 hours.

— Kimberly Park
